- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, apply a 1–3 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.  
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days with sentiment swings), reduce forecast magnitude by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend, apply a downward bias correction of 0.5–1.5% to avoid “over-optimism” in the model.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.2 → +0.3), apply a 2–3 day smoothing filter to avoid oscillation-induced overfitting.
